title: Diagnosis: system logs, safe mode and recovery

videos.script: Monday morning. The daily disk report that the server writes every night has not appeared for a week, and nobody noticed. A reception PC restarts itself twice a day. A Mac shows a grey screen after an update. Three problems, and the temptation with each is to start trying things. {{monday}} Diagnosis is the opposite of trying things. It is asking, in order, what exactly happens, since when, what changed, and what the system itself recorded about it. Every system keeps a record, and it is usually more precise than anybody's memory of what they clicked. {{record}} Where the machine stops also narrows the search. A computer that reaches the login screen can tell you what went wrong in its logs. One that stops earlier needs a smaller system to help it: safe mode, which loads almost nothing, or recovery, which starts something else entirely. {{where}} In this lesson you will read Linux's journal, and follow a failed report from its missing file to the line that explains it. You will see why the service said everything was fine when it was not, and fix it. Then Windows' Event Viewer and repair tools, safe mode and recovery on all three systems, and a method that works whichever system is in front of you. {{steps}} The Linux transcripts come from lesson 3's server. The Windows and Mac tools are described, not run. {{honest}}
